questions.key_step: Orthogonality test (C1C2^2=r1^2+r2^2) then kite area r1*r2
questions.justification: One familiar move (orthogonal circles) after finding centres/radii; short.

questions.key_step: Auxiliary circle x^2+y^2=9, line AB meets it again; area 1/2*OA*y_P
questions.justification: Routine chain: intercepts, circle, solve quadratic, area; no insight needed.

questions.key_step: Quadratic in y, sum of roots from centroid gives m, then c
questions.justification: Routine chain of standard steps; options allow checking.

questions.key_step: Normal at pi/3 to x-axis: normal form gives a=2p, b=2p/sqrt3
questions.justification: Three standard steps (normal form, intercepts, area); angle-with-y-axis conversion is the only trap.

questions.key_step: Tangent at B is perpendicular to radius so angle ABC=90 degrees, AC=r*sqrt2
questions.justification: One geometric observation plus Pythagoras; short but needs the picture.

questions.key_step: Right angle at (0,3) makes circumcentre the mid-point of hypotenuse; eliminate m
questions.justification: Two ideas linked (right-triangle circumcentre, tangent slope form) followed by an elimination.

questions.key_step: T=S1 for xy=2 chord, then tangency c=a/m to y^2=24x
questions.justification: Two conics linked (rectangular hyperbola mid-point chord + parabola tangent); locus then directrix reading.

questions.key_step: Centres at distance sqrt(R^2-2^2)=4 from the focus on opposite sides of the latus rectum
questions.justification: One familiar geometric move (half-chord, Pythagoras).

questions.key_step: Substitute y^2=3x^2 in the circle to get x^2=b, y^2=3b; put on the ellipse
questions.justification: Short routine algebra chain, quadratic in b, apply b>4.

questions.key_step: CC1+CC2=r1+r2 gives an ellipse with foci (0,0),(2,0); test options
questions.justification: Standard locus recognition then ellipse parameters; options make the check easy.

questions.key_step: Angle AOB=90 so AB is a diameter; tangent at O is 2x+y=0; two distances
questions.justification: Routine chain: diametral circle, tangent at origin, point-line distances.

questions.key_step: Inscribed square parallel to axes: vertices centre +- r/sqrt2; compare four distances
questions.justification: One familiar move; no solution printed in the PDF but the route is short and direct.

questions.key_step: b^2=ac makes ax^2+2bx+c a perfect square; common root -sqrt(c/a) in the second equation
questions.justification: Two chapters (parabola on y=1 + G.P./A.P.); the perfect-square observation is the key idea, then a short algebra step.

questions.key_step: Parametric P(3t^2,6t), Q has x=3t^2/4, y-intercept of NQ is 4t
questions.justification: Parametrisation then slope and intercept; routine and options help.

questions.key_step: Perpendicular radius vectors: find R from the perpendicularity (or use 1/OP^2+1/OR^2 constant)
questions.justification: Needs a computation of R (or an unfamiliar identity) and the diameter doubling; precision in fractions.

questions.key_step: Focal chord parameters t,-1/t; length a(t+1/t)^2 fixes t; section point M; test four options
questions.justification: Chain of 4-5 stages (focal chord, acute-angle selection, section formula, perpendicular line, option test).

questions.key_step: Family (point-circle)+lambda*(tangent) through (4,0)
questions.justification: Standard family-of-circles technique; two short stages.

questions.key_step: Parametrise X on the arc; area is a quadratic in t; maximise
questions.justification: Routine determinant area plus calculus maximisation.

questions.key_step: A on the perpendicular bisector y=x of BC, so AO is the height; area=h^2/sqrt3
questions.justification: Three routine steps (symmetry, find A, equilateral area).

questions.key_step: Common tangent y=mx+4/m with circle condition gives m=+-1; contact points Q,R
questions.justification: Two tangency conditions combined, contact-point formulas, then distance; an easier cousin of 2023-P1-Q2.
